home.heroEyebrow: European association for the Digital Product Passport
home.introText: DigiPass:Europe is a non-profit technical-scientific association. Its members build, regulate, research and use Digital Product Passports; the association gives them one table, ten working groups and a direct line to the institutions that write the rules.
home.missionTitle: What the statutes ask of us
home.ecosystemTitle: One passport, six kinds of reader
home.ecosystemLead: The passport travels with the product. Every actor along the way writes to it or reads from it; the association exists so that they all agree on how.
benefits: A seat in the working groups
Shape recommendations, guidelines and position papers before they are published.
Monthly tracking of the ESPR, delegated acts and standards, read by the people who must apply them.
Industry, research, technology providers, standards bodies and public authorities in one directory.
Test your implementation against others before a customer or a market-surveillance authority does.
home.wgLead: Members choose their groups; each elects its chair and vice-chair and adopts a yearly work plan.

about.title: About DigiPass:Europe
about.lead: A non-profit technical-scientific association, founded to be Europe’s networking hub for the Digital Product Passport and the interface to the institutions and standards bodies that define it.
about.objectivesLead: The statutes list the means by which the association pursues its purpose (§ 3 a). The working groups and services on this site are how they are put into practice.
about.governanceLead: The bodies of the association are defined in § 8 of the statutes. Office holders will be published here once elected; no names are listed before then.
about.boardNote: The Board consists of at least five natural persons, the founding members, plus any further members elected by the General Assembly. Names and functions will be published after the constituent meeting.
about.wgLeadershipNote: Each working group elects a chair and a vice-chair. All positions are currently open.
about.statutesText: The Articles of Association (German, with English translation) govern purpose, membership, bodies and dissolution.
about.conditionsLead: Admission and termination follow § 4, § 6 and § 7 of the statutes.
about.transparencyLead: Non-profit status brings obligations. These are the ones the statutes make binding.
about.reportsText: The Board reports to the General Assembly on the previous year’s activities, submits accounts and prepares the budget (§ 9 l). Annual reports will be published here from the first full association year.

membership.title: Membership
membership.lead: Open to companies of every size, universities, research centres, public bodies, technology providers, associations and qualified individuals. Membership categories are those of the statutes; fee levels are proposals for the Board and the General Assembly.
membership.proposedBanner: The fees below are a strategic proposal. They are not adopted prices: the General Assembly sets membership fees and fee categories (statutes § 10 c 8) and the Board assigns each member to a category (§ 4 g). The Board may modify this structure at any time.
membership.categoriesLead: Four categories exist (§ 4 a). Every tier on this page is a fee level inside one of them.
categories: Authorities, legal entities and other corporations from Austria or abroad. Only the officially named representative votes: 2 to 4 votes depending on fee category (§ 10 g).
Persons with a completed relevant education or at least four years of relevant experience. One vote; eligible for the Board.
Students and pupils of higher educational institutions. May attend the General Assembly; no vote.
Recognised experts, and persons honoured for financial support or many years of merit. Honorary members vote and pay no fee.
membership.supporterNote: Supporter is a subscription, not a membership category.
membership.benefitsLead: Benefits are what the association offers; governance rights come from the statutes alone. Sponsorship and partnership never add votes or control.
membership.howLead: The statutes set the procedure (§ 4 f–g, § 6 a). The online application prepares the file; the Board decides.
membership.feesInclude: Fees cover the association year (calendar year); new members pay pro rata by commenced month (§ 6 a). Honorary members are exempt (§ 6 b).
